ambiguities.evidence: On PDF page 18, immediately before the statement labeled Theorem 2.6.3, the source says to apply 'Theorem 2.6.3 for aᵢXᵢ instead of Xᵢ.'
ambiguities.impact: This is a circular numbering reference as printed. The displayed derivation and placement identify Theorem 2.6.2 as the intended predecessor; the typo should be recorded, not treated as a different mathematical hypothesis.
ambiguities.issue: The paragraph deriving the weighted theorem cites Theorem 2.6.3 itself.

ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 2.6.3 on PDF page 18 imposes no condition K‖a‖₂>0; its allowed weights include a=0, and Definition 2.5.6 allows K=0 when all variables are almost surely zero.
ambiguities.impact: For a=0 or K=0, the ordinary-real expression c t²/(K²‖a‖²₂) is undefined (and is 0/0 at t=0). The corresponding event probabilities are clear, but the source does not specify an arithmetic convention or explicit case split.
ambiguities.issue: The displayed denominator may be zero although the theorem quantifies over every a∈ℝᴺ and every t ≥ 0.

contract_plain_english: There is an unspecified positive universal constant c such that, for independent mean-zero sub-gaussian Xᵢ, every deterministic real weight vector a and every nonnegative threshold obey a two-sided tail bound for ∑aᵢXᵢ with denominator K²‖a‖²₂, where K is the maximum ψ₂ norm of the summands. This is obtained by applying the unweighted theorem to aᵢXᵢ, using ψ₂ homogeneity and bounding the exact squared-norm sum by K²‖a‖²₂. The ψ₂ norm remains the exponential-square infimum norm; the MGF bound is only an equivalent proof device up to absolute constants. The source contains a self-referential theorem-number typo in the derivation paragraph and leaves the zero-denominator cases a=0 or K=0 unstated.

source_evidence.anchor: Theorem 2.6.3 (General Hoeffding's inequality), statement and displayed weighted bound
source_evidence.observation: For independent, mean-zero, sub-gaussian X₁,…,X_N, a=(a₁,…,a_N)∈ℝᴺ, and every t ≥ 0, the source states P{|∑ᵢ₌₁ᴺ aᵢXᵢ| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−c t²/(K²‖a‖²₂)), where K=maxᵢ‖Xᵢ‖_{ψ₂}.

The weighted result is introduced by applying the preceding general inequality to aᵢXᵢ in place of Xᵢ; the paragraph prints 'apply Theorem 2.6.3', a self-reference in the introduction of Theorem 2.6.3, where the mathematical derivation indicates Theorem 2.6.2.

source_evidence.location: PDF page 16; printed page 27 (surrounding definition explicitly cross-referenced by the locator's Definition 2.5.6 anchor)
source_evidence.observation: The source defines ‖X‖_{ψ₂} = inf{s > 0 : E exp(X²/s²) ≤ 2}; it records the two-sided tail bound and, under mean zero, the ordinary-MGF bound with absolute constants c,C > 0. This norm definition is homogeneous, so ‖aᵢXᵢ‖_{ψ₂}=|aᵢ|‖Xᵢ‖_{ψ₂}.

source_evidence.observation: The unweighted result is proved through independence, the mean-zero MGF estimate, ψ₂/MGF equivalence, and the ψ₂ tail estimate; applying it to aᵢXᵢ gives ∑‖aᵢXᵢ‖²_{ψ₂}=∑aᵢ²‖Xᵢ‖²_{ψ₂}≤K²‖a‖²₂.

binders: A positive integer N (implicit in the notation X₁,…,X_N and ℝᴺ).
Real-valued random variables X₁,…,X_N on a common probability space.
A deterministic real weight vector a=(a₁,…,a_N) ∈ ℝᴺ.
A real threshold t with t ≥ 0.
conclusions: With K := max_{1≤i≤N} ‖Xᵢ‖_{ψ₂}, P{|∑ᵢ₌₁ᴺ aᵢXᵢ| ≥ t} ≤ 2 exp(−c t²/(K²‖a‖²₂)).
definitions_and_conventions: The sub-gaussian norm is ‖X‖_{ψ₂} := inf{s > 0 : E exp(X²/s²) ≤ 2}, i.e. the scale associated with Proposition 2.5.2(iv).
K is defined from the family by K=max_{1≤i≤N}‖Xᵢ‖_{ψ₂}; it is not an additional free MGF parameter.
‖a‖₂²=∑ᵢ₌₁ᴺaᵢ², and homogeneity of the ψ₂ norm gives ‖aᵢXᵢ‖_{ψ₂}=|aᵢ|‖Xᵢ‖_{ψ₂}.
The symbol c denotes a positive absolute (universal) constant, not a theorem input and not a specified numerical value; the book's equivalences permit absolute constant factors.
The absolute value is outside the entire weighted sum, so the claim is a two-sided tail bound.
The mean-zero MGF estimate is used as an equivalent ψ₂ property in the proof and does not replace the theorem's ψ₂-norm formulation with a fixed variance/MGF proxy.
hypotheses: Each Xᵢ has mean zero: E Xᵢ = 0.
Each Xᵢ is sub-gaussian in the sense of Definition 2.5.6 / Proposition 2.5.2.
implicit_context: All probabilities and expectations refer to the common underlying probability space; a is deterministic.
The same absolute-constant convention used in Theorem 2.6.2 and equations (2.14)–(2.16) is inherited by the weighted theorem.
The source states the inequality for every t ≥ 0 and every a∈ℝᴺ without separately assuming K‖a‖₂>0 or declaring an extended-real division convention.

details: Apply Theorem 2.6.2 to Yᵢ:=aᵢXᵢ, which remain independent, mean zero, and sub-gaussian.
The exact unweighted denominator for Yᵢ is ∑aᵢ²‖Xᵢ‖²_{ψ₂}; it is bounded above by K²∑aᵢ²=K²‖a‖²₂, producing the displayed specialization up to the absolute constant.
The source's introductory self-reference to Theorem 2.6.3 is a numbering defect; the logical predecessor used is Theorem 2.6.2.
The bound is uniform over N, all families satisfying the three hypotheses, every deterministic a∈ℝᴺ, and all t ≥ 0.
The displayed rate uses K=maxᵢ‖Xᵢ‖_{ψ₂} and the Euclidean norm of a, with one unspecified absolute c.
The weighted form is a specialization of the ψ₂-norm theorem for the scaled variables aᵢXᵢ.
Behind that theorem, independence factors the MGF, mean zero enables (2.16), and Proposition 2.5.2 plus Definition 2.5.6 convert MGF control back to ψ₂-norm and tail control.

details: The denominator K²‖a‖²₂ vanishes when a=0 or K=0.
The source still quantifies over every a and t ≥ 0 and gives no convention for division by zero, so the printed quotient has an unstated boundary interpretation.

undebatable_constraints: Retain mutual independence, individual mean-zero assumptions, and sub-gaussianity of every Xᵢ.
Retain arbitrary deterministic real weights a∈ℝᴺ, the two-sided event |∑aᵢXᵢ| ≥ t, and the universal range t ≥ 0.
Retain K=maxᵢ‖Xᵢ‖_{ψ₂} and the denominator K²‖a‖²₂; do not replace K with a chosen MGF parameter or omit the Euclidean weight norm.
Retain the source's unspecified absolute-constant convention: c is universal and positive, not a fixed numeric constant silently selected by the formalizer.
Preserve the weighted-specialization logic from Theorem 2.6.2 applied to aᵢXᵢ, including ψ₂ homogeneity and the comparison ∑aᵢ²‖Xᵢ‖²_{ψ₂}≤K²‖a‖²₂.
Do not silently exclude a=0, K=0, or t=0. Because the source supplies no zero-denominator convention, a formal statement must expose how the degenerate boundary is represented.
Preserve the ψ₂ formulation and the source's equivalence-up-to-absolute-constants proof sketch; do not silently recast it as a theorem for one fixed MGF parameterization.
